def _validate_identity(self, role, response, payload):
        returned = response.get("model")
        require(isinstance(returned, str), "missing_response_model")
        normalized = "typesafe/" + returned.removeprefix("typesafe/") if role == "jev" else returned
        require(normalized in self.config.response_models(role, payload["model"]), "response_model_mismatch")

requested = request["model"].removeprefix("~").removeprefix("typesafe/")
    returned = response["model"].removeprefix("typesafe/")
    require(re.fullmatch(r"jev-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+", returned) and
            (requested == "jev-latest" or returned == requested or
             returned.startswith((requested + ".", requested + "-"))), "response_model_mismatch")

candidate.text:
jev_decide.validate_response alone: ACCEPTS. requested="jev-1.13", returned="jev-1.13.2"; returned.startswith(requested+".") is True ("jev-1.13." prefix matches), so the regex+prefix check passes with no error.

However, Gateway.call also runs transport._validate_identity, which is stricter. For role=="jev" it normalizes the returned model to "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" and checks membership in config.response_models("jev", ...) = {"typesafe/jev-1.13", "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"}. "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" is not in that set, so require(...) fails and raises "response_model_mismatch".

Net result: the Gateway records error code "response_model_mismatch" for this call — identity validation rejects the response even though jev_decide's own validator would have let it through.

data.summary: jev_decide.validate_response alone accepts "jev-1.13.2" as a valid response to a request for "jev-1.13" (startswith requested+"." branch). But Gateway.call also enforces transport._validate_identity, which normalizes to "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" and requires exact membership in config.response_models("jev",...) = {typesafe/jev-1.13, typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917}. That membership check fails, so the Gateway records error code "response_model_mismatch".
claims: jev_decide.validate_response: requested="jev-1.13" (after stripping typesafe/ prefix), returned="jev-1.13.2"; returned.startswith(requested+".") is True, so this validator alone accepts the model with no error.
Gateway.call does not rely on jev_decide alone; transport._validate_identity runs as part of the identity validation layer and is stricter (exact-set membership vs. prefix matching).
_validate_identity for role=="jev" normalizes returned model to "typesafe/"+returned = "typesafe/jev-1.13.2".
config.response_models("jev", payload["model"]) returns exactly (jev_model,)+jev_model_aliases = ("typesafe/jev-1.13", "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"); "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" is not a member.
Because the membership check fails, require(...) raises "response_model_mismatch", which is the error code the Gateway records for this call.

Assumption: Gateway.call invokes _validate_identity (or an equivalent identity check) on every response in addition to any model-specific validator like jev_decide.validate_response; this is inferred from the identity.py excerpt and the request framing, not independently confirmed from Gateway.call's source in this evidence set.
Assumption: jev_model_aliases is read from the default RunConfig as shown (only one alias, "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"), with no other aliases added at runtime.
